newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey says killed 54 Kurd rebels in two days.
newsitem.headline: Turkey says killed 54 Kurd rebels in two days.

text.p: Security forces killed 54 Kurdish guerrillas in fighting over the weekend in southeastern Turkey, the emergency rule governor's office said in a statement on Monday.
The statement said troops, backed by air power, killed 33 members of the rebel Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) in the province of Van, near Turkey's border with Iran.
In separate clashes, security forces killed another 12 guerrillas in the southeastern province of Hakkari and a further three in Sirnak province, it said.
There was no mention of military casualties.
Officials at the governor's office in Diyarbakir earlier said six guerrillas had been killed late on Sunday in the southeastern province of Bingol, two of them women.
The clashes on Turkish soil take place as Turkish forces are engaged in a six-week operation against the PKK in neighbouring northern Iraq, which the rebels use as a base for raids into Turkey.
State-run Anatolian news agency on Monday reported the funeral of one soldier killed in fighting with the PKK but did not say when or where he died.
More than 24,000 people have been killed in the conflict between Turkish security forces and the PKK, fighting for 12 years for autonomy or independence in the mainly Kurdish southeast.
